SGP: RELEVANT PROPERTIES
• Student growth percentiles (SGPs) are a norm-referenced
 quantity.

• SGPs use (quantile) regression to approximate the conditional
 density associated with each students achievement history.

• Similar to residualized gain scores.

• SGPs are uncorrelated from year-to-year.

• For a random sample of students, the median SGP associated
 with the group is expected to be 50.

• “Treatment effects” would be associated with deviations from 50.

THE TRANSITION TO PARCC

• SGP analyses are norm-referenced and don’t require a vertical
 scale to be conducted. Depending upon whether results are
 disseminated, a likely cause of confusion: “How can you calculate
 growth across two different tests?”

• Other PARCC SGP states we’re conducting analyses for:
 Massachusetts, New Jersey, Colorado

• The Center conducted meetings with both SBAC and PARCC
 consortium members discussing issues related to calculating and
 using growth during assessment transitions.

CONCLUSIONS

• SGPs provide an easy way for states to comb through the data
 and examine the impact that various “treatments” have on the
 outcomes of students.

• Some states (e.g., MA) immediately looked at this metric while
 others weren’t sure how to examine.

• Need to give more thought to helping states use the data that
 they have available to quickly test relevant hypotheses.
